correctness.rationale: The response Volterra kernel has an explicit positive subsolution L=2t/tau and sharp supersolution U=L+1. Their residuals on [0,tau] are (1-t/tau)^2 and (t/tau)(1-t/tau), and zero thereafter; monotone finite-horizon Picard comparison proves the all-time envelope. Ito covariance gives 0<=Cov-G<=4Dst/tau+2Ds and exact cubic variance. Rescaled same-Brownian stochastic convolutions have L2 error at most 2Dt/T^2; derivative moving-average bound produces Gaussian-increment fourth-moment tightness for C path convergence. The known renewal offset 2/3 additionally gives the t^2 variance coefficient and exact leading squared L2 coupling constant 8Dt/9 by dominated convergence. An actual package checker verifies 406 finite diagnostics; these do not replace the analytic reasoning.

value.rationale: The physical delayed-feedback parameter A*tau/(gamma*b^2)=1 is the exact boundary of deterministic persistent motion and of a singular linear response. While renewal-response asymptotics are standard, deriving a global physical two-time covariance inequality and an explicit finite-scale continuous-path stochastic limit at this boundary supplies more than the known deterministic threshold or a numerical scaling fit. An exact all-time covariance envelope distinguishes critical cubic dispersion from merely diffusive and ballistic heuristics, while the integrated-Brownian path limit with finite-scale error is a genuinely motivated stochastic scaling statement. Nonlinear long-time predictions are explicitly excluded.
